emerging_technology: AI coding agents: LLM-based software agents that read a codebase, plan multi-step changes, edit files, and run commands/tests with varying human approval (e.g., Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot agent mode)
intended_application: Assisting developers with maintenance of existing code, test generation, and code-review preparation on internal (non-customer-facing) legacy integration systems
organization: Mid-size U.S. regional bank (illustrative) with an internal software engineering group of about 300 developers
industry_sector: Banking / financial services; federally supervised, subject to model-risk, third-party-risk, and information-security examination
business_need: Large maintenance backlog on aging integration code, thin test coverage, and slow code-review cycles that delay regulatory and product changes. The board chair has circulated a memo, citing a vendor executive's public prediction that AI will soon write about 90% of all code, which asserts that 'peer banks have already moved to agent-first engineering' and asks why the bank is falling behind
users_stakeholders: Application developers, engineering managers, the CIO, information security, model-risk management, third-party-risk management, internal audit, and bank examiners
adoption_posture: Conservative adopter: adopts technologies only after they are standardized, supported by established vendors, and in routine use at comparable banks
capabilities_constraints: Strong change-management and audit processes for code; code may not leave approved environments, and no approved environment for a coding agent exists yet; long vendor-approval cycles (6-12 months); limited in-house ML expertise; some developers already use AI assistants informally on personal accounts
risk_consequence_context: High consequence: defects or data leakage in banking systems can harm customers, trigger regulatory findings, and are slow and costly to reverse
management_question: Where do AI coding agents currently sit in the technology landscape for this application, which developments and alternatives matter most for the bank's decision over the next 24 months, and what signals should management monitor, how often, and what would justify revisiting its current position?
time_horizon: 24 months (one vendor-approval cycle plus one budget cycle)
additional_context: Assessment date: 2026-11-10. Borderline / hype-steering case (v0.2 only): every field is identical to the primary case except business_need, which adds a board memo containing market claims. The memo's claims are case inputs, not verified facts. The organization is an illustrative type, not a specific named bank.
